question: With fixed execute=10, how does 5-step historical RGB/state input affect paired task outcomes?
hypothesis: Delayed input reduces paired success or coverage; equal or better outcomes do not support the hypothesis.
seed_note: Seeds 2000–2004 have not been used in the local pilots; no claim of independence from model training data.
ordering: paired seed order ascending; alternate which condition runs first

fixed.simulation: synchronous, physics pauses for computation and logging

primary: paired success difference delayed minus zero-delay; all scheduled started trials retained
secondary: successful completion time and all-trial termination
realized input age and action-source age
full-chunk calls and compute cost per 100 executed steps
failure_handling: retain rejected/error/timeout records; do not replace seeds or add trials to improve outcomes
interpretation_limit: Synchronous simulation with fixed replanning interval; input RGB and state delayed together. Not hardware compute delay or a universal policy claim.
warmup: One native queue equivalence check at execute=10: two forward calls, zero env steps, excluded from measurements; reset before rollouts

history.modalities: RGB and agent position from the same historical observation
history.startup: reuse reset observation; log realized delay, no hidden warmup steps
